scenes.title: Sunlight
scenes.purpose: Start at the bright surface and show light being used up: colour by colour.
scenes.visual: A water plate with caustics and light beams; the surface and a boat leave the top of the frame as the camera sinks; a five-band colour strip loses red, orange, yellow and green in turn, and blue is left, glowing.

transition_out.continuity: a vertical push reads as the camera continuing downward

scenes.narration: The sea looks bright from the surface. But sunlight does not travel far. Red light is filtered out first, and blue goes deepest.

layout.landscape: surface leaving frame top, strip right, gauge left

scenes.title: Twilight
scenes.purpose: Mark the twilight zone and make the dimming felt.
scenes.visual: The camera continues down; light shafts die; a pale jelly drifts up through marine snow; the depth gauge brackets 200 to 1,000 m.

transition_out.continuity: a slow dissolve: depth as a change of state, not a place

scenes.narration: Below two hundred metres, there is rarely any significant light. This is the twilight zone, and it reaches down to one thousand metres.

layout.landscape: jelly lower-right, zone label lower-left, gauge left

scenes.title: Pressure
scenes.purpose: Make pressure felt as weight, not as a fact.
scenes.visual: A field of horizontal lines slowly closes as a counter climbs from 1 to 1,090 atm and the gauge runs to 10,900 m; the numeral warms to amber as it climbs.

transition_out.continuity: an iris opens like a porthole onto the dark

scenes.narration: Going down, the pressure builds. It rises by about one atmosphere for every ten metres. At the bottom of the Challenger Deep, that adds up to roughly eleven hundred atmospheres.

layout.landscape: big numeral centre-left, line field right

scenes.title: Midnight
scenes.purpose: Turn the surprise into a picture: no sunlight, yet three in four make light.
scenes.visual: A hundred dim dots; seventy-six ignite one by one, each with a soft bell; then 76% resolves beside them with its scope.
scenes.narration: Below one thousand metres, no sunlight reaches at all. Yet in seventeen years of video off California, about three in four animals seen made their own light.

layout.landscape: dot field right, big percentage left

on_screen_text: of animals seen made their own light

scenes.title: Light
scenes.visual: Everything dims; the dots drift aside and one line of type remains.
